newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fu Hui directors to sell 29.7 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: Fu Hui directors to sell 29.7 pct stake.

text.p: Fu Hui Jewellery Co (HK) Ltd said on Wednesday three of its directors have agreed to sell their entire holding of 113.70 million shares or 29.68 percent stake in the company to third parties at HK$0.55 per share.
Fu Hui said managing director Chu Kwok Fai and executive director Chan Shui Chu have agreed to sell a total of 55 million shares or a 14.36 percent stake to investor So Sik for HK$30.25 million.
So Sik is the chairman and 66.7 percent controlling shareholder of property firm Triplenic Holdings Ltd.
Chu also agreed to sell 27.45 million shares or 7.16 percent of Fu Hui to So's brother So Kim Fung for HK$15.10 million, the company said.
Another Fu Hui executive director, Lau Hau Wah, has agreed to sell 31.25 million shares or 8.16 percent of the company to Anworld Ltd for HK$17.19 million.
Anworld is an investment firm equally owned by Yau Nin Seung and Lau Lap Tak. Both are business partners of So Sik.

On completion of the deals on December 16, the purchasers -- including So Sik's wife, who has held 568,000 shares or 0.15 percent of Fu Hui since 1993 -- will become the single largest group of shareholders with 114.27 million shares or 29.83 percent of the company.
The deals are conditional on the Securities and Futures Commission granting the purchasers a waiver from an obligation of making a general offer for outstanding Fu Hui shares.
Fu Hui said the purchasers were independent of Fujian Jewellery Import and Export Corp, a China stated-owned company holding 25.79 percent of Fu Hui.
"There is no arrangement, understanding or agreement between them whatsoever in respect of their respective shareholdings in the company following completion," Fu Hui said.

"There will not be any material change in the core jewellery business of the group in the coming few years," Fu Hui said. "At present, none of the purchasers has any specific expansion plan for the group or any plan to inject assets into the group."
Fu Hui also engages in one property investment project in Hong Kong and two property and hotel investment projects in China.
Trading in Fu Hui shares, which was suspended on November 15, will resume on Wednesday.
